item.title: Cooler Master GPU Shield Gets Lower Price and Warranty Period in EU
item.description:
A month after Cooler Master launched its GPU Shield 12v-2×6 power cable monitoring solution in the US, it has finally released the safety accessory in the EU, where it received a €29.99 price tag—compared to $49.99 in the US.

Along with the lower price, however, Cooler Master has also reduced the warranty period on the GPU Shield adaptor cable from three years in the US and China to just two years in the EU—just barely covering the minimum threshold for legally mandated warranties in the EU, but still longer than the one-year warranty granted for the international version of the GPU Shield. The GPU Shield adaptor cable is available via Cooler Master directly, and it does not appear to be available on sites like Amazon just yet.

item.title: HP EliteBoard G2a Keyboard Computer Launches with Eyewatering Price and AMD Ryzen AI 400 APUs
item.description:
HP revealed the EliteBoard G2a keyboard PC at CES 2026, promising "next-generation local AI power in a keyboard-sized form factor." Now, 10 months later, HP has released the updated EliteBoard G2a, revealing pricing and some of the keyboard and underlying PC specs, in the process. The G2a features either the updated AMD Ryzen AI 7 Pro 450 APU or its smaller Ryzen AI 5 Pro 435 counterpart. The cheapest version of the HP EliteBoard G2a, which packs a Ryzen AI 5 Pro, 16 GB of DDR5-5600 memory, and 512 GB of PCIe Gen 5 SSD storage, comes in at $3,028, while the SKU with the Ryzen AI 7 Pro 450 APU paired with 32 GB of memory and a 512 GB SSD, comes in at $4,167.

The small form factor PC is capable of drawing 65 W over USB Power Delivery, and the only I/O it features is a single USB4 port and a single USB Type-C 10 Gbps port. The EliteBoard G2a also features built-in dual speakers and comes bundled with an HP 675M wireless mouse. The keyboard component of the mini PC is a membrane keyboard, not mechanical, and it follows what appears to be an 1800 layout, and it has white backlighting. Fortunately, the EliteBoard G2a uses SODIMM RAM, so it's upgradeable in the event that you want 32 GB of RAM but don't want to pay HP's upgrade cost.

item.title: Xbox Responds to AI-Powered Game Mods and Projects with "Xbox Labs"
item.description:
In the weeks leading up to publication, a number of software engineers and modders have decompiled and recompiled games, unlocked mods, and accelerated game emulation, resulting in everything from a browser-based Fallout: New York game to full PlayStation 5 game ports using AnyPS5. It seems as though Microsoft has now taken notice of the uptick in these AI-accelerated game mods and unofficial port projects and launched Xbox Labs in response.

In a recent email shared by Xbox CEO, Asha Sharma, she explains that the rapidly accelerating pace of game and mod development that has been a result of these AI "experiments challenge long-held assumptions about our industry," and that "it is easy to see the possibilities in making great games easier to access, giving old games new life and allowing more players to become creators and co-creators." The motivation behind Xbox Labs appears to be to get out ahead of these AI projects and "turn emerging ideas into things our players and developers can experience."

item.title: Steam and Windows Games Now Run Locally on Android, Cyberpunk 2077 Hits 60 FPS
item.description:
An open-source app called DroidDeck is letting Snapdragon-powered Android devices run Valve's Steam client and Windows PC games on the device itself, with no streaming from a PC or the cloud involved. As VideoCardz reports, YouTuber ETA Prime tested it on a RedMagic 11 Pro with the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 and 16 GB of memory, where Cyberpunk 2077 ran at around 60 FPS on medium settings. Skyrim Special Edition hit a similar figure at 720p, while Hogwarts Legacy was tougher on the phone and sat around 40 FPS even with lower settings and FSR.

Other solutions like Steam Link stream games from another PC, whereas DroidDeck runs them on the device itself. It loads Valve's ARM64 Linux Steam client in Big Picture mode as a regular Android app, and Windows games go through Valve's ARM64 Proton with x86 translation. Projects like Armada instead replace Android with SteamOS entirely, and DroidDeck needs neither that nor root access. It also handles GPU driver switching, AMD FSR and Snapdragon GSR upscaling, and frame generation through Lossless Scaling.

item.title: RimWorld's Switch to In-House Engine Promises Up to 400% Performance Boost
item.description:
Despite launching in early access in 2013, RimWorld's developer, Ludeon Studios has just started a switch away from the Unity game engine to its own in-house Waylith engine with update 1.7. In a new blog post, the developer notes that the switch away from Unity could result in performance improvements of "2-4×," while claiming an identical gameplay experience.

In the studio's in-house testing, game load time, startup time, world and map generation, and general tick-per-second performance all saw significant performance improvements. A stress test with a "late game colony" saw a performance improvement of 2.2×, although the studio didn't exactly share test parameters beyond that. Load times of a mod pack with 1,500 mods also improved from 14 minutes to 6 minutes. The studio notes that individual performance improvements on the new engine will depend on PC specs, but those are promising improvements if scaling holds up.

item.title: Xbox Won't Survive Without New IP, Warns CEO Asha Sharma
item.description:
Xbox CEO Asha Sharma told staff at an internal town hall last week that the division needs new IP to survive, according to transcripts obtained by Windows Central from multiple sources. Sharma apparently said Xbox will keep betting on its biggest franchises, though she also wants the studios to keep making new games, and she framed that second part as a matter of survival. Sharma did tell The New York Times earlier this month that Xbox is not for sale, so it seems the plan is a smaller Xbox that still takes some creative risks. Here's what she reportedly said:
We're backing our strongest franchises. I want our great games to become great global billion-dollar franchises. I would also like to see us continue to create enduring new IP. We will not survive if we only revive on the past. We have to find new ways, and courage, to have invention on new IP, that reaches new sets of audiences.

item.title: God of War Laufey Collector Box Costs £129.99, Game Not Included
item.description:
Sony has opened pre-orders for the God of War Laufey Collector Box on its UK PlayStation Store, priced at £129.99. Despite the name, the box does not include the game in any form, and the store page states plainly that God of War Laufey is sold separately. Buyers instead get a light-up resin statue of Faye, a 51-card Oracle Deck with custom illustrations on every card, and a mini artbook of concept art put together by the development team. Orders are capped at one per customer, and the listing carries a February 16, 2027 date, the same day the game launches on PlayStation 5.

The Faye-led spin-off was first tipped back in April, and Santa Monica Studio confirmed the February release at San Diego Comic-Con in July. The Standard Edition sells for $69.99 and the Digital Deluxe Edition for $79.99, and there is no word of a traditional collector's edition that bundles the game. That is quite a change from God of War Ragnarök, whose $199.99 Collector's Edition came with access to the game on both PS4 and PS5. Of course, Sony isn't alone here, since Rockstar's $399.99 Vice City Collection box for GTA 6 also leaves the game out. It looks like players who want both the statue and the game will have to buy them separately.

item.title: GTA 6 Reportedly Coming to PC in Q1 2027
item.description:
Rockstar is planning to bring GTA 6 to PC sometime in the first quarter of 2027, according to a new report from GamesBeat. The outlet cites four industry sources familiar with the studio's plans, all of whom asked to stay anonymous. If accurate, PC players would get the game between January and March 2027, just a few months after its November 19 launch on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. Rockstar still hasn't announced a PC version, and PC was left out of the launch plans from the start. Interestingly, if the timing pans out, that would be a much shorter wait than last time. GTA 5 hit consoles in September 2013 and only reached PC in April 2015, roughly 19 months later.

This could matter for the roleplay ecosystem too, since FiveM, the framework behind most GTA 5 roleplay servers, runs only on PC, and GTA 6's online mode is already tipped for 2027. Of course, early PC launch windows have surfaced before that haven't exactly panned out. A Corsair executive floated an early 2026 launch last year, a comment Corsair later called speculation, and VGC's Andy Robinson suggested last month that the PC version might show up sooner than people expect. A Q1 2027 release would also arrive before Take-Two's fiscal year closes on March 31, 2027. Until Rockstar says something, readers are advised to treat this as a well-sourced rumor and not a confirmed date.

item.title: NVIDIA RTX Spark Game Ready for Dozens of AAA Titles at Launch, Including DLSS 5 and Anti-Cheat Support
item.description:
NVIDIA today announced that its new RTX Spark superchip that will power the next-generation of AI-native PCs, will be Game Ready for dozens of AAA games at launch on Windows 11, providing an uncompromising gaming experience that's maxed out for 1440p. The RTX Spark superchip features a 20-core Grace CPU and a GeForce RTX Blackwell iGPU featuring 6,144 CUDA cores. NVIDIA is closely collaborating with Microsoft and the various game developers to ensure not just Spark-native ports of popular titles, but also seamless translation of games to the RTX Spark platform for both the system- and graphics APIs.

A key announcement here is that NVIDIA is working with developers of competitive online games to ensure that their anti-cheat solutions work seamlessly with RTX Spark. Modern anti-cheat solutions rely heavily on kernel-mode interactions with hardware to ensure trust, something that has the potential to break in scenarios where games originally developed for Windows x64 machines are made to run on Windows Arm64 machine through translation layers. NVIDIA's developer collaboration ensures that the hardware-end of the anti-cheat trust-chain remains intact, and you should be able to play your favorite online games such as Counter-Strike 2, Dota 2, Fortnite, Marvel Rivals, NARAKA: BLADEPOINT, Rocket League, RUST, THE FINALS, War Thunder, World of Tanks, and more.

item.title: NVIDIA Unveils "Preset C "DLSS Frame Generation with up to 35% Faster Generation
item.description:
NVIDIA has updated its DLSS Frame Generation algorithm to be faster and more efficient. In the latest NVIDIA App beta update, rolling out today, the company introduced "Preset C," the fastest Performance Mode for DLSS Frame Generation. NVIDIA demonstrates that this mode can make frame generation up to 35% faster on the GeForce RTX 5060, with minimal trade-offs in image quality. This improvement applies to the GeForce RTX 40-Series, GeForce RTX 50-Series, and RTX Spark.

According to NVIDIA, there are two models for DLSS: Multi-Frame Generation and Frame Generation. The first model uses a standard AI approach that inputs motion vectors and depth to understand how two rendered frames are constructed. The second model employs optical flow for in-game elements like UI and ray tracing. Today, NVIDIA replaced this optical flow model with a much faster and lighter AI algorithm that boosts FPS across DLSS Frame Generation, Multi-Frame Generation, and Dynamic Multi-Frame Generation. This new model is available for download through the NVIDIA App beta update, so ensure you're running the latest beta version to try out the "Preset C" setting.

item.title: NVIDIA DLSS 5 Gets 2x Performance Boost with 20% Less VRAM Usage
item.description:
NVIDIA's continuous optimization of software and its technology stack has yielded another great improvement. The latest DLSS 5 update, scheduled for October 16, will deliver another 2x performance boost, meaning that previously DLSS 5-optimized workloads will literally run twice as fast. Alongside this significant performance uplift, NVIDIA promises that in 4K gameplay with DLSS 5 enabled, the neural rendering technology will use 20% less VRAM, leaving more room for game textures to load without DLSS 5 interfering with capacity or hogging resources. NVIDIA updates its DLSS by running a continuous loop on top of an internal supercomputer that constantly optimizes DLSS technology for performance, efficiency, and visual fidelity. Specifically for this week's DLSS 5 update, NVIDIA states that the company used a combination of systematic pipeline optimizations and neural model refinements to achieve that 2x performance boost.

Originally in late August, we saw that the leaked DLSS 5 file was roughly a 148 million parameter model. Our analysis turned out to be accurate, and we see that, according to NVIDIA, the DLSS 5 October update shrinks the footprint of this model by another 24% to roughly 118 million parameters, meaning that our original estimation was correct. Consequently, the smaller model scales memory usage almost linearly and cuts VRAM usage by about 20%. Compared to the initial launch in mid-March, when the DLSS 5 was showcased on two GeForce RTX 5090 GPUs, we see that NVIDIA managed to scale the performance by 10x in the span of a couple of months.

Its expansion layout includes PCIe 5.0 slots, two M.2 storage connectors, and a legacy PCI slot for older industrial hardware. For wireless connectivity, we see that Decanta's platform supports expansion through an M.2 E-Key socket that supports Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6.x modules. item.title: AMD Showcases Its Next-Gen EPYC "Verano" CPU, Up to 192 Cores and LPDDR5X Memory
item.description:
AMD showed off its next-generation EPYC "Verano" server CPUs during CEO Dr. Lisa Su opening keynote at the 2026 OCP Global Summit. The new CPU is the first EPYC processor to support LPDDR5X memory via SOCAMM2 modules. Now AMD is mirroring rival NVIDIA's Vera CPU that already uses SOCAMM2 modules. The "Verano" processor sits within the EPYC 9006 "LP" family and is built on the same TSMC 2 nm process as the already-launched EPYC "Venice". While AMD "Venice" is the first EPYC processor based on Zen 6 architecture, "Verano" is optimized for AI tasks in agentic AI racks. For this, AMD plans to pair them with its own Instinct MI500 GPUs via xGMI connectivity at up to 112 Gbps. It will run on the new SP8 platform rather than Venice's SP7. When we first heard about "Verano", AMD indicated that the upcoming CPUs will feature up to 72 cores on a single-socket platform. However, that has now been updated to up to 192 cores.

From the initial information available, this could mean either a single large chip or a dual 96-core configuration. More details came from System360Cheese on X, who reported that the chip shown featured eight Zen 6 CCDs alongside two large IO dies and four LPDDR5X memory controllers. The CCDs appear smaller than those in Venice's Zen 6C design, suggesting these are the standard 12-core Zen 6 dies rather than the denser 32-core Zen 6C variants. The announcement follows AMD's earlier reveal of the Helion agentic AI rack, an Open Compute Project spec-designed system that Verano is expected to be integrated. Availability is targeted for 2027.

item.title: Intel Refers to its 3D V-Cache Analog as "BFC"
item.description:
Intel is introducing its analog to AMD's 3D V-Cache technology with its upcoming Core Ultra Series 4 "Nova Lake" desktop processors. We've known for over a year now, that the company is introducing SKUs with enlarged last-level caches. Technical docs leaks have until now referred to this technology as "bLLC," which simply meant "big last-level cache." We weren't sure if bLLC would be used as a marketing name for the tech, and it turns out, we're right. Apparently, Intel is going with "BFC" as the brand-extension for processor models featuring bLLC.

Video is H.264 decoded on the CPU, so there's no HDR for now, and bitrate sits at around 10 to 12 Mbps at 1080p. Some early testers reportedly ran into macroblocking, pink artifacts, and DualSense vibration issues. It's the latest in a busy stretch for PS5 homebrew, following emulators that run Nintendo Switch games, load PS2 discs, and even get Halo 2 running on the console. The newly named D-Series GPU features a total of 32 Xe3P cores, 256 XMX engines, 32 MB of unified L2 cache, and up to 480 GB of LPDDR5X memory with up to 1.5 TB of memory bandwidth. Intel rates it for up to 1.3 PetaFLOPS of FP8 performance, with support for formats ranging from FP4 to FP64. A media engine with four encoders and four decoders is also included, which could assist with multimodal workloads where video generation and understanding is a must. The card comes with 160 GB memory configuration out of the box, which is exclusive to Intel-branded "Crescent Island" graphics cards, while the company allows its ODMs to equip the card with up to 480 GB of LPDDR5X memory for maximum VRAM capacity.

What is particularly interesting about the Xe3P is its pipeline. The XMX engines have been redesigned from the four-deep systolic design on the regular Xe3 to 16-deep processing on the Xe3P. Additional details include FP4 data format support alongside FP8, as well as large register files of 1 MB per core and L1 cache of 512 KB per core. In total, there are 256 Vector engines and 256 of the new XMX engines, each divided into groups of eight per Xe3P core. Additionally, in the Xe3P, there are no graphics processing elements to output imagery, as the silicon is designed purely for AI inference workloads that require long context and agentic tasks.

item.title: GlobalFoundries Returns to Advanced-Node Race With 7 nm-Class FDX Fusion
item.description:
Back in the now distant 2018, the semiconductor industry had three major players in contract leading-edge node manufacturing: TSMC, Samsung, and GlobalFoundries. At that time, Intel did not accept external clients. However, as node design became increasingly expensive—requiring multi-billion dollar investments—and more complex, with many players encountering yield and manufacturing difficulties, GlobalFoundries announced that it was stopping its 7 nm node development indefinitely. This left only two companies in the leading-edge race, but GlobalFoundries continued to develop unique semiconductor solutions that did not focus on smaller transistor sizes.

Today, the company is back at a similar stopping point but with a unique solution called FDX Fusion, based on fully-depleted silicon-on-insulator (FD-SOI) technology. Unlike traditional CMOS, GlobalFoundries takes substrate isolation a step further by creating a fully insulating layer beneath the channel. This enables highly specialized capabilities, such as ultra-low-power in-memory computing, seamless integration of embedded non-volatile memory (like eMRAM), and highly efficient dense logic designs. With FDX Fusion, GlobalFoundries claims 7 nm-class node characteristics in terms of size and twice the transistor density of the first-generation 22FDX node, which was designated as a 22 nm-class design.

item.title: Intel "Panther Lake" Reportedly Gets Up to 20% Price Hike, Older Generations Also Impacted
item.description:
Intel is reportedly preparing for a significant price increase across its silicon designs, according to supply chain sources cited by Commercial Times Taiwan. The first to experience this price hike is the latest "Panther Lake" processor generation, built on the Intel 18A node, with an increase ranging from 15% to 20% depending on the SKU. Intel reportedly made these adjustments on September 1, but consumer price increases have not yet been observed, or it may take a few more weeks for the old supply to clear. This supply-side price hike doesn't mean that Intel is directly changing its consumer pricing, but rather adjusting the pricing for major laptop OEMs such as Acer, ASUS, Lenovo, Dell, and HP. With a potential 20% price hike, this could translate to a few dozen US dollars more for the OEMs. Laptop manufacturers are likely to pass these increased costs onto consumers, especially given the current challenges with memory and storage pricing, which are already squeezing margins.

The reported price hikes don't stop there. The "Meteor Lake" and "Arrow Lake" processor families are also expected to see price increases, with reports indicating a 5% to 10% hike for these two generations, depending on the SKU. Intel sources silicon from both TSMC and its internal foundry, but the demand for silicon in the form of CPUs is skyrocketing in the age of AI, making price increases likely. Consumer demand remains, but much of the available CPU manufacturing capacity, both internally and externally, is being absorbed by agentic AI workloads, which are pushing server configurations to a 50:50 ratio of CPUs to GPUs.

item.title: Modder Boots Googlebook OS on Apple Silicon Macs
item.description:
Googlebook laptops arrived only a few weeks ago, and Googlebook OS is already running on hardware Google never built it for. Developer Skylar Taylor-Barrick has published gbos-vm, an open-source project that boots the OS inside a GPU-accelerated virtual machine on Apple Silicon Macs, with Chrome working. Apparently, the install script downloads Google's own recovery image for the Dell XPS Googlebook, an ARM64 build based on Android 17, replaces the hardware-specific vendor partition with virtual device components from Google's Cuttlefish project, and boots it under QEMU.

The Dell is one of the Snapdragon X-powered Googlebooks, so its Arm image runs on the Mac's hypervisor without emulation. That also means Intel Macs are out. Googlebook OS renders through Vulkan while Macs use Metal, so the project passes Vulkan calls through MoltenVK. The README asks for 16 GB of RAM, 60 GB of free storage, Xcode command line tools, and the Android SDK with NDK, plus a hefty 9 GB of downloads. First boot takes about 45 seconds on an M5 MacBook, which is the only machine the developer lists as tested.

item.title: Ghost of Yotei Reaches Gameplay on PS5 Emulator SharpEmu, Performance Still Needs Work
item.description:
Ghost of Yotei has become the latest PlayStation 5 exclusive to get past its menus on PC. Developer Foued (@foufouadi_) shared footage on X of Sucker Punch's 2025 samurai game running in a modified build of SharpEmu, the experimental PS5 emulator whose playable list is mostly small indie and retro-style titles. The clip shows the start menu, a 3D environment loading in, and protagonist Atsu moving around. The results, however, are far from playable. Foued clarified that the video was sped up, and the real frame rate is reportedly around 1 to 2 FPS, with geometry and texture errors on top. Apparently, performance work will come later.

A separate screenshot shows the fight against The Snake, the game's first boss, at 10.9 FPS on a GeForce RTX 4090 and Ryzen 7 7800X3D, with some effects still rendering incorrectly. Another attempt through AnyPS5, which relinks PS5 executables instead of emulating the console, is further behind, with the game world reportedly loading at roughly 3.4 frames per minute. Ghost of Yotei follows Marvel's Wolverine, which booted on KytyPS5 late last month and has since reached around 20 FPS. The same emulator also ran the PS5 version of GTA 5 at up to 60 FPS. Interest in these projects picked up after Sony moved away from PC ports of its single-player games, with a planned Ghost of Yotei port reportedly among those scrapped. A playable build is still a long way off, though it's reasonable to expect quick improvements given how fast these emulators have moved.

item.title: Steam Tops 43.5 Million Concurrent Players, New All-Time High
item.description:
Sundays are designated as free time, and gamers are confirming that today, as Steam has reportedly hit 43.5 million concurrent players, representing a new all-time high. On Sunday, October 11, at exactly 14:00 UTC, 43.5 million gamers were online to chat, play, and enter their favorite digital worlds for entertainment. This marks a new all-time high for the platform, which has broken countless records in the past. Interestingly, one might expect this record to occur during the holiday season when most people have extra time to play. However, it seems that the number of gamers on Steam is increasing even during regular times. Several factors could be contributing to this, including gamers trying out new hardware purchased during the holiday season, seeking discounts, or simply browsing the platform to see if anything interesting is happening.

At the same time, the number of players in-game was recorded at 14.46 million active gamers, meaning the rest were using the platform to browse, chat, or perhaps do some game shopping. Nonetheless, 43.5 million concurrent Steam users is a massive achievement. With many new AAA game titles being released recently, alongside Steam being the platform of choice for publishing games, it is currently experiencing demand that keeps piling on. More platforms like the Steam Frame VR headset will also help boost that figure even higher, and as gamers are using all available devices to transform them into mini Steam Decks, the surge is expected. item.title: Microsoft Warns Windows Update Will Stop Working on Unpatched PCs Next Year
item.description:
Microsoft is replacing the certificates that Windows PCs use to confirm they are talking to genuine Windows Update servers, and machines that miss the changeover will stop receiving updates. The company announced the rotation on October 8, and the current certificates expire on May 17 and June 19, 2027. Most users apparently won't have to do anything, since the replacements ship inside the regular monthly security updates. Windows 11 25H2 and later, including the recently launched 26H2, need no action. Windows 11 24H2 needs the September 2025 security update or newer, while other supported Windows 11 and Windows 10 versions need the July 2026 update or later before June 19. Windows 10 Enterprise 2019 LTSC, Windows Server 2019, and Windows Server 2016 face the earlier May 17 deadline.

Microsoft says devices on unsupported versions "will lose access to Windows Update services and won't receive any updates as a result," and its only advice is to upgrade. For home users, that mostly points at Windows 10 PCs that were never enrolled in Extended Security Updates (ESU) after the OS reached end of life in October 2025. Those machines probably never got the July 2026 patch. Microsoft extended ESU coverage to October 12, 2027, so it looks like enrolling and installing the offered updates before June should bring the new certificates along. The warning also comes months after Microsoft began refreshing Secure Boot certificates that were due to expire in late June 2026. Readers are advised to check their update history for a cumulative update from July 2026 or later.

item.title: Activision DMCA Takes Down Vibe-Coded Call of Duty Browser Ports
item.description:
Activision has reportedly issued a DMCA takedown against a set of unofficial Call of Duty browser ports made by developer Luckey Faraday. Faraday announced it on X, saying the publisher went after him "for porting CoD games to the browser," that every related post was removed, and that every game is now offline. He also asked whether he is the first "vibe coder" to get a DMCA notice from a major gaming company. The notice itself hasn't been shared publicly, so the exact claims are not known, and Activision doesn't seem to have commented so far. The projects in question are Claude of Duty: Vibe Slops II, a Black Ops 2 multiplayer recreation, and Kino der Toten, a browser version of Black Ops Zombies. Both ran on Three.js and were built with the help of AI coding agents.

Vibe Slops II offered free-for-all matches against six bots on Hijacked and Nuketown 2025, while the Zombies project had Kino der Toten fully playable solo. The project pages state that the maps, models, and animations were exported from the original PC games, which probably didn't help Faraday's case, even with both labeled as non-commercial fan projects. The Kino der Toten repository was still accessible on GitHub at the time of writing, so it looks like the takedown hit the hosted games and the posts promoting them. It comes less than two weeks after Take-Two sent a cease-and-desist to the modder behind the GTA 5 Switch port, and shortly after a free browser port of Halo: Combat Evolved showed up.

item.title: KINGPIN Says a Connector Dispute With NVIDIA Derailed EVGA's Last Flagship Card
item.description:
Vince "KINGPIN" Lucido has blamed NVIDIA for the troubled launch of the EVGA GeForce RTX 3090 Ti KINGPIN, the last graphics card to carry his name. In the first video on his new Overclocking Kingpin YouTube channel, the overclocker said he wanted the card to have two 12VHPWR power connectors, while NVIDIA wanted it limited to just one. The disagreement, in his words, "really screwed up the production timeline", and he also holds it responsible for how few units were made afterward. The card did eventually ship with both 16-pin connectors when it went on sale for $2,500 with a bundled 1600 W power supply, about three months after the RTX 3090 Ti itself came out. This is only Lucido's side of the story, and it isn't clear why NVIDIA pushed for a single connector.

In September 2022, EVGA ended its partnership with NVIDIA and stopped making graphics cards, with CEO Andrew Han pointing to a souring relationship between the two companies. Every card in development was canceled, KINGPIN models included. Lucido is now working with ASUS, which sent over the hardware shown in the video, although no ASUS-made KINGPIN card has been confirmed. He did lay out one condition for such a card: the PCB and power delivery have to let the GPU reach its full potential under liquid nitrogen without the buyer modifying anything. An earlier plan with PNY never produced a card, and Lucido ended up skipping the RTX 50 generation entirely.

item.title: GTA 6 Leaker Claims to Have Full Build, Threatens to Release It Unless Take-Two Apologizes
item.description:
The notorious leaker known as Cyberleek is now threatening to release what is claimed to be a playable build of GTA 6 ahead of the game's November 19 launch. According to a post on the leaker's own website, the build supposedly includes the full story mode, playable through to the end credits. The threat comes with two conditions. The build would apparently go out if a meme coin tied to the leaker reaches a $30 million market cap, and the coin reportedly sits roughly $26 million short of that mark. The post also offers Take-Two a way to avoid the release, stating: "Take-Two gets one way out: physical disks and a public apology."

That is a reference to GTA 6 launching without a disc, as boxed copies are set to ship with a download code. Neither Take-Two nor Rockstar appears to have responded publicly so far, but Rockstar did acknowledge the leaks in late August. Tying the threat to a coin's market cap also gives the post an obvious financial angle, since the attention alone could move the price, so the claim is probably best treated with caution. The claim has not been independently verified, there is no date attached to it, and it may well turn out to be a bluff. Readers are also advised to stay away from the leaker's site and from any files that claim to be the full GTA 6 build, as there is no way to tell what they actually contain.

item.title: PS2 Discs Now Load on Jailbroken PS5 Consoles Through PS5SX2 Emulator
item.description:
Developer Sword has added physical disc support to PS5SX2, a native port of the PCSX2 PlayStation 2 emulator for jailbroken PlayStation 5 consoles. The feature arrived as a beta in version 2.01 on October 10, a day after Sword showed it off on X with a clip of a PS2 disc going into a PS5. Contrary to how it may appear at first, the game does not seem to run straight off the disc. According to the release notes, PS5SX2 copies the disc to storage the first time it is inserted and then launches the game from that copy. Sword adds that this has only been tested on one original PS5.

That said, the PS5's optical drive apparently cannot read CDs, so PS2 games that shipped on CD are out, at least through the internal drive. Version 2.02, out later the same day, adds an experimental, off-by-default option that builds on a community contribution for reading PS2 discs from a USB DVD or Blu-ray drive, which should help Digital Edition owners. The emulator renders at up to 6x the PS2's native resolution, although the README warns that some games are too heavy for 6x on a regular PS5. Sword isn't stopping at the PS2 either, confirming that PS3 disc support is planned for an RPCS3 port that is in the works. The timing is notable, as Sony plans to stop producing discs for new PlayStation games from January 2028.

item.title: AMD Reportedly Raises GDDR6 Prices for Board Partners
item.description:
AMD has reportedly raised the price of the GDDR6 memory it supplies to its board partners, with the change said to be in effect since October 1. The claim comes from a post on the Chinese forum Board Channels, and it doesn't mention a percentage or a dollar figure. AMD sells its GPUs to add-in board (AIB) partners bundled with memory, so a costlier kit usually ends up in the retail price of the finished card. The timing matches the higher suggested Radeon prices in China reported earlier this week, where the RX 9070 went up by the equivalent of $104 and the RX 9060 XT 8 GB by $45, while the RX 9070 XT was left untouched.

NVIDIA, however, apparently hasn't sent its partners a similar notice for GDDR7 this time, and the same post suggests the company may not touch memory pricing again this year. That would be a small relief for GeForce buyers, although NVIDIA already raised GDDR6 and GDDR7 kit prices in July, and the RTX 5090 was tracked at 136% above MSRP globally in early September. AMD's partners have been through this a few times in 2026 already. A 10% hike on Radeon GPU kits was reported for July, and in September there was word of another 10% increase across GPUs, chipsets, and possibly CPUs, tied to rising TSMC wafer costs. AMD hasn't confirmed the latest increase, and we don't know how much or how soon store prices outside China will move.

item.title: Yuzu Launches Customizable KLP Lamé Keycaps for Ergonomic Mechanical Keyboards

Yuzu, the custom keycap maker, has just added the open-source KLP Lamé keycap profile to its portfolio of customizable keycaps, alongside the already available Cherry, KAM, PFF, and PBS profiles. KLP Lamé is a heavily sculpted ergonomic keycap profile designed specifically for use in ergonomic keyboards. Much like Cherry profile, KLP Lamé has different heights and angles for each row, making it easy to orient yourself on your keyboard. As is the case with other Yuzu keycaps, the KLP Lamé keycaps are 1.5 mm PBT with dye-sublimated legends.

Given that ergonomic keyboards, and especially split ergonomic keyboards, rely heavily on customization and layers, it seems as though it would be an ideal use case for a service like Yuzu, since no two split layouts are the same once they have been adapted to each individual user's needs. The keycap editor allows you to pick your own fonts, colors, symbols, and even upload custom images onto keycaps. The KLP Lamé keycaps come in both Choc and MX spacing, covering a variety of available ergonomic mechanical keyboards, but not mixed Choc spacing and MX stems, which excludes users running keyboards like the MoErgo Go60 with Choc V2 switches.

item.title: NVIDIA Reportedly Ending the RTX 5090, Reserves GB202 Silicon for Workstation GPUs
item.description:
NVIDIA has reportedly stopped allocating GB202 silicon to the GeForce RTX 5090, according to leaker MEGAsizeGPU (@Zed__Wang) on X. "No more GB202 for 5090, confirmed," the leaker posted, adding in a follow-up that "all future GB202 supplies are RTX Pro exclusive." GB202 is the largest "Blackwell" graphics chip, and the RTX 5090 doesn't even max it out. The same chip powers the 96 GB RTX PRO 6000 with 24,064 CUDA cores, as well as the recently unveiled RTX PRO 5500, which pairs the RTX 5090's 21,760 CUDA cores with 84 GB of memory. Apparently, NVIDIA would rather put every GB202 it gets into those far pricier workstation cards. The company hasn't confirmed any of this as of the time of writing.

A second leaker, hongxing2020, posted "5090 EOL, 5080 24GB ready" alongside an apparent factory notice saying NVIDIA will no longer sell any RTX 5090 model, China-market D variants included. The same notice says an RTX 5080 24 GB will become the top GeForce card and the 16 GB version will be discontinued. That sounds a lot like the RTX 5080 SUPER, which was rumored with 24 GB of GDDR7 on the same GB203 chip, although it isn't clear if the two are the same card. SUPER cards reportedly reached board partners in July, only to be put on hold over GDDR7 pricing. As for the RTX 5090, I doubt NVIDIA would formally call this an end-of-life (EOL) move, since the chips are simply being redirected to a more profitable product line.

item.title: Sony Patent Describes Stream Viewers Controlling a Cursor on the Streamer's Screen
item.description:
Sony has been granted a US patent for a system that lets livestream viewers point things out on a streamer's screen and even change what happens in the game. Titled "Adaptive screen share pointer and reactions during gameplay," US 12752199 was filed in October 2023 and appears to have been issued on October 6. A viewer gets a cursor that shows up over the streamer's gameplay, and its look changes with the game being played. The patent gives examples like marking a boss's weak point or showing where to aim a shot. Viewers could also drop stickers on the screen, or send emoji reactions that the streamer feels as vibration through a controller, VR headset, or phone.

It goes further than pointing, however. The patent describes game actions reserved for viewers who aren't controlling the character, such as triggering a lever or revealing a hidden item, and publishers would define these through an SDK. Only one cursor may appear at a time, with control passed between viewers through a queue based on engagement points. Streamers could earn a virtual trophy from the reactions they receive, while viewers get tiered rewards of their own. Consoles from Sony, Microsoft, and Nintendo are all listed as client devices.

The analytics firm estimates that Gears of War: E-Day sold around 230,000 copies since its launch, with around 168,000 of those copies coming from Steam and 62,000 of them coming from Xbox. Despite this, though, Xbox players still accounted for almost three quarters of the game's $37 million in revenue.

The big differentiator here is that 1.7 million gamers played E-Day via an Xbox Game Pass subscription, and 722,000 subscribers paid an additional $30 for the Premium Edition Game Pass upgrade, which gave them early access to the game. The end result is that, even though few gamers actually bought Gears of War: E-Day, Xbox accounted for an estimated $26 million in revenue, where Steam only garnered $11 million.

item.title: Xbox and PlayStation US Sales Sink as Average Console Prices Hit Record Highs
item.description:
Xbox and PlayStation console sales in the US are having a rough 2026, according to new Circana data that analyst Mat Piscatella shared on Bluesky. For the year 2026 through August, Xbox hardware unit sales are down 33% year over year, while PlayStation units are 25% lower. That puts Xbox at an all-time low and PlayStation at its lowest point since 2013. As one might expect, it looks like pricing is the main culprit. Buyers paid an average of $529 for a new Xbox console this year, 26% more than a year ago, and $597 for a PlayStation, up 20%. Both are record highs for the US, and Piscatella says price sensitivity is becoming a real problem.

The decline follows a string of price hikes tied to the memory and storage shortage. Sony raised the PS5 Pro to $899.99 in April, Microsoft pushed the Xbox Series X to $799.99 on August 1, and Nintendo moved the Switch 2 to $499.99 in September, a hike analysts had warned about back in January. August itself was weak, with total hardware unit sales falling 15% to 559,000, the lowest August total since 2013. The Switch 2, however, remains the best-selling console of 2026 in both units and dollars. Piscatella said the US hardware market hasn't been "in a more precarious position since the early 80s." He thinks GTA 6's big launch might ease some of these declines, although that depends on console availability and pricing.

item.title: Xbox Names Former Reddit Product Chief As CEO of Minecraft Studio Mojang
item.description:
Xbox has hired a social media product veteran to run Mojang. In a memo to staff on October 8, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma said Maria Angelidou-Smith, most recently chief product officer at Reddit, will join as CEO of Mojang and Minecraft. She starts on October 19 and reports directly to Sharma. Angelidou-Smith replaces Kayleen Walters, who moves over to lead XP, the new Xbox division for film, TV, merchandise, and live experiences. Walters had run Mojang since February 2025, and Xbox says Minecraft went from 350 million copies sold to more than 425 million in that time.

Angelidou-Smith's background is in community products, with no game studio role mentioned. According to the memo, she spent nearly a decade at Meta, where she led Facebook Groups along with Events, Creators, Search, Profile, and Monetization. She later led product and technology at HR software company Personio and joined Reddit in November 2025. item.title: AnyPS5 Achieves Full PS5 GPU Shader Instruction Translation
item.description:
A few weeks ago, we reported on an intriguing project called AnyPS5, which aims to bypass emulation entirely and run PlayStation 5 games natively on Windows and Linux. Today, the project reached a significant milestone by successfully translating 100% of the PlayStation 5 GPU shader instructions. This achievement means that the "Oberon" graphics processing engine within the PS5 has been fully decoded. All 1166 GPU shader instructions, based on the RDNA 2 GPU IP, are now covered under the AnyPS5 project. The project relinks PS5 executables into the host system's native format and reimplements the console's system libraries for dynamic linking, similar to Wine or Proton. Since the PS5 already runs on x86-64 Zen 2 hardware, which is similar to a modern PC, AnyPS5 skips CPU emulation and recompiles shaders into SPIR-V for Vulkan instead.

What is particularly interesting is that once GPU shader instructions are translated, all the system needs are PS5 libraries so they can be dynamically linked from a native PC port. This means the PS5 game will see the exact same system calls on a PC as it does on the console. However, the system libraries have not yet been fully translated, with current statistics showing 84.81% of system libraries translated. There are exactly 3034 system libraries native to the PS5, and currently, 2573 have been translated. Once the remaining 461 libraries are translated, we can expect PS5 games to run natively on PCs, bypassing emulation layers entirely.

item.title: AMD Engineer Details Zen 6 IBS Memory Profiler
item.description:
AMD has detailed the IBS Memory Profiler, a little-discussed hardware feature in its upcoming Zen 6 processors. AMD engineer Bharata Bhasker Rao presented it at the Linux Plumbers Conference (LPC) 2026 in Prague on October 5. Instruction-Based Sampling (IBS) is AMD's existing profiling hardware, and Zen 6 adds a separate, lighter instance that only samples data memory accesses. Each sample hands the kernel the physical address of the access and shows whether the data came from DRAM or external memory such as CXL. That matters on tiered-memory servers, where Linux has to find frequently used ("hot") pages on slower CXL memory and move them to DRAM. AMD's EPYC 9006 "Venice" chips support memory expansion via CXL 3.1.

Linux currently finds those pages by scanning page tables and trapping page faults. AMD wants to feed the profiler's samples into pghot, a proposed kernel subsystem for hot page tracking. The results, however, are a mixed bag. On a test system with 256 logical CPUs and 256 GB of CXL memory, XSBench ran at 4.57x over a no-tiering baseline against 1.18x for the current method, and Graph500 hit 3.17x against 2.34x. Redis saw no gain, and NAS BT landed slightly behind. Per-folio promotion cost fell from 26.1 to 15.8 microseconds in an overhead test, though that benchmark finished about 5% slower. These are AMD's own numbers, and the slides list no virtualization support for the profiler. The pghot patches are still in development, and EPYC Venice is in production with cloud deployments expected later this year.

item.title: Sony Patent Describes Bosses That Learn From Your Reaction Times and Retries
item.description:
Sony Interactive Entertainment has a new patent application out that describes using machine learning to change how NPCs and bosses behave, based on how the person holding the controller plays. Titled "AI-adapted non-player character for video game system" (US 2026/0295429 A1), it was filed on March 31, 2025, published by the USPTO on October 1, and spotted by Patentlyze. The system collects player data and game data from an encounter with an NPC, feeds both into a machine learning model, and uses whatever the model returns to modify that character.

The data Sony lists is quite granular. On the player's side, it covers reaction time to boss attacks, the success rate of dodges, blocks, and parries, the weapons and consumables used, and even the number of retries. On the boss's side, it tracks attack patterns and how often the player avoided or countered them. Combat is only part of it, since the filing also mentions dialogue, appearance, and NPC voices that shift in pitch and volume. Sony says this content could be generated before a game runs, in real time during play, or afterward, so a boss that adapts mid-fight is one of several scenarios covered.

HPE (NYSE: HPE) today announced the first four of its HPE ProLiant Gen13 Servers powered by 6th Generation AMD EPYC Server processors. The new systems expand compute, memory, and I/O capabilities to help enterprises accelerate agentic AI and inference, analytics, virtualization, simulation, and modeling while strengthening security, simplifying operations, and providing reliability across distributed IT environments.

As AI systems evolve from generating insights to taking autonomous action, trust becomes a prerequisite for scale. McKinsey's 2026 AI Trust Maturity Survey found that nearly two-thirds of respondents cited security and risk concerns as the top barrier to fully scaling agentic AI. Within this evolving landscape, HPE ProLiant Gen13 helps customers address security and operational barriers with a trusted infrastructure foundation that combines HPE iLO 8 innovations for automatic protection, infrastructure trust, and post-quantum readiness with enhanced visibility and control from HPE Compute Ops Management.

item.title: AMD Shares Its Progress with Agentic PCs
item.description:
AMD held a press briefing to share how its "Agentic PC" push is going, and it brought a fair number of figures along. Apparently, the company has shipped over half a million Agentic PCs across more than 50 designs, alongside tens of millions of AI PCs across more than 250 designs. Of course, the term "Agentic PC" is AMD's own. It covers any PC whose CPU, GPU, and NPU can run AI agents locally, and AMD says Ryzen AI Max+ systems with 64 GB of memory or more give the best experience. The Ryzen AI Max 400 series is pitched as the "next-gen Agentic PC" for 2026, and most of the briefing focused on its flagship, the Ryzen AI Max+ PRO 495 "Gorgon Halo" with 192 GB of memory.

item.title: SK hynix Reportedly Faces Difficulties in HBM Hybrid Bonding, Trailing Samsung
item.description:
According to a process development engineer at SK hynix's future technology research institute, who spoke with Damnang, SK hynix is reportedly facing challenges in developing hybrid bonding technology for its HBM memory. These issues are significant enough that SK hynix has not yet begun production of samples, while Samsung has reportedly already sent out samples of HBM manufactured using hybrid bonding to customers. If true, this represents a major setback for SK hynix, whose HBM has held the top spot in global market share by revenue. This could potentially lead to a loss of market share among customers who require higher capacities, better performance, and more advanced technology from their HBM suppliers.

For those unfamiliar, hybrid bonding creates a permanent bond between two silicon chips using embedded metal bumps that are fused together to form a single chip. Multiple dies or entire silicon wafers can be connected by stacking the back ends of two chips together. This technology eliminates traditional chip bumps and directly bonds copper interconnections between the two chips. Essentially, hybrid bonding can create shorter distances, reducing latency and improving performance, lowering signal distortion, and offering many other benefits.

item.title: Samsung Foundry to Manufacture Anthropic AI ASIC on 2 nm Node
item.description:
Samsung Foundry may be on the verge of securing a significant deal with AI lab Anthropic to manufacture AI accelerators. According to the latest report, Anthropic is developing its custom AI accelerator on Samsung's SF2 2 nm node, which will initially be produced in a lower volume of around 200,000 chips. The design and implementation of this ASIC are being handled by Broadcom, targeting around 4,000 TOPS of INT8 compute, with a TDP of 1,300 W per chip. This will be supported by either 192 GB of HBM3E or even 288 GB of HBM3E, if the design allows. The current production volume is low, as ASIC projects are typically counted in millions of chips. However, Anthropic is likely evaluating the project's viability, which requires a complete custom infrastructure with networking, rack design, power supply, cooling, and many other factors.

The current Samsung SF2 node is built using Low-NA EUV lithography and is manufactured in South Korea, with a new facility soon to be established in Taylor, Texas. For packaging these chips and integrating them with HBM, Samsung is likely to employ its I-Cube technology, which rivals TSMC's CoWoS and allows for 2.5D packaging. Combined with the 2 nm dies, Samsung can position itself as a serious manufacturing plant for external customers and slightly close the gap with TSMC and its contract manufacturing business.

item.title: Intel to Continue Working on Terafab, Confirms CEO Lip-Bu Tan
item.description:
A few days ago, after news broke that Elon Musk and his Terafab project are looking to start working with TSMC, we were left in the dark about Intel's role in the project. However, we are finally getting confirmation straight from Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan that the collaboration will continue, despite TSMC being in talks with Terafab. Previously, we learned that the Terafab project wants to license the 14A node from Intel and possibly other technologies, which would kickstart production at the Texas campus where Elon Musk plans to initiate another wave of semiconductor manufacturing on American soil.

The talks with TSMC began when managers at Terafab started questioning whether Intel could deliver on its promise of node excellence with 14A, and TSMC showed interest. However, Intel is not out of the picture, as Intel IP will be the base of Terafab for now. TSMC will not operate any capacity on its own, and Elon Musk confirmed on X that everything will be built and operated by the Terafab team, with TSMC having the option to sublease some capacity. This means that TSMC will not be lending any node IP to Terafab but could instead aid with knowledge work in building and maintaining a fab, gaining some extra manufacturing capacity in return.

item.title: Xbox Helix Will Be "a Great Console First" With Portable Play in Mind, Says CEO
item.description:
Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has reportedly told staff that the next-generation "Project Helix" hardware will lead with a home console, with portable play apparently coming as part of the same lineup. The remarks come from an internal town hall, and Windows Central says it obtained and verified a transcript. Helix was already known to be a "family of devices" instead of a single box, but this is the clearest hint so far about what else is in that family. Here's what she said:
We are moving to a family of devices for Gen-10. There is not one device that fits all. We will certainly have a great console first, but we also know that many players will be on the go. There are some things that we are the best in the world to manufacture, and there are other things that we will partner on. So, we will be sharing more about that as our plans develop. The operating system is starting to look really good. We're very excited about this.
